entities.summary: Joseph ben Ephraim Karo was a Sephardic Jewish rabbi who lived in 16th-century Portugal and Spain, and is regarded as the preeminent halakhic authority of his time. Born around 1488, Karo traveled extensively throughout the Mediterranean, including visits to North Africa and the Holy Land. He eventually settled in Safed, Palestine, where he wrote the Beit Yosef, a comprehensive codification of Jewish law that would later be popularized as the Shulhan Arukh. Karo's work had a profound impact on Jewish law and practice, shaping the tradition for centuries to come. His influence can be seen in the many rabbis and scholars who followed in his footsteps, including the great Ashkenazi rabbi, Moses Isserles. Karo's legacy extends beyond the Jewish community, as his work on Jewish law and tradition has influenced the development of Western legal thought and continues to shape the study of Jewish history and culture. Despite his significant contributions to Jewish law and scholarship, Karo's life was marked by personal tragedy, including the loss of his son and his own eventual death in 1575. Yet, his work continues to be studied and revered by scholars and laypeople alike, a testament to the enduring power of his ideas and legacy.
